script.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.

terra.problem: The text says the leaders feared a riot, not that they wanted to stay away from a crowd.
The oven comparison does not match the action of checking a schedule: a full oven and no timer do not explain a calendar problem.
The dough comparison does not make sense: a batch of dough is not something one cracks open, and dough can be put back.
The text does not say Simon watched from the table or that the perfume was meant for Jesus alone.
The text does not say whether the woman went to Jesus' feet or what happened to the jar afterward.
It predicts that thirty pieces of silver will appear later in this story. Mark's account does not give that amount.
The text does not say the chief priests were somewhere else while the woman anointed Jesus.
The text does not establish that nobody else at the table was talking about Jesus' burial.
Identifying the Twelve as Jesus' chosen disciples is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
Explaining 'told' as specifically spoken narrows the promise beyond what the text says.
'Right again' assumes the baker answered correctly before, which Papa Dorin has not been told.
'That's the whole offer' asserts that there were no other details or terms, which the text does not establish.
The passage mentions a promise of money but does not establish that no title or throne was offered.
